question:
A 43-year-old woman who recently immigrated to the United States from the Philippines one month ago
undergoes a tuberculin skin test, which shows 12 mm of induration at 48 hours. She denies
experiencing symptoms such as fever, chills, weight loss, night sweats, or cough. She reports no
known exposure to individuals with active tuberculosis and has never received the bacille
Calmette-Guérin vaccine. A chest radiograph reveals no lymphadenopathy or parenchymal
abnormalities, and her HIV test is negative. What is the most appropriate management for this patient?
Answer Choices: (A) Screen for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis before initiating therapy (B) Begin
treatment with rifampin (C) Observe without treatment unless symptoms develop (D) Administer a
booster dose of the tuberculin skin test (E) Order an interferon-gamma release assay (F) Prescribe a
combination of isoniazid and pyrazinamide for 2 months (G) Perform sputum acid-fast bacilli (AFB)
smear and culture (H) Repeat the chest radiograph in 6 months (I) Begin treatment with isoniazid for 9
months (J) Repeat the tuberculin skin test in 3 months
 A. Observe without treatment unless symptoms develop
B. Begin treatment with rifampin
C. Screen for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis before initiating therapy
D. Repeat the tuberculin skin test in 3 months
E. Perform sputum acid-fast bacilli (AFB) smear and culture
F. Administer a booster dose of the tuberculin skin test
G. Order an interferon-gamma release assay
H. Repeat the chest radiograph in 6 months
I. Prescribe a combination of isoniazid and pyrazinamide for 2 months
J. Begin treatment with isoniazid for 9 months
